title: On-demand SLA & quota-driven observability add-ons pilot
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Experiment to validate a friction-minimized enterprise add-on bundle that combines: (1) a short-term, on-demand premium SLA (SLA on-demand) that can be enabled per-route or per-application, (2) quota-driven observability retention credits that let customers top up retention for specific routes, and (3) a compliance pack gating flow driven by the enterprise security questionnaire. Goal is to find a flexible packaging model that increases ARPU for mid-market and enterprise accounts while keeping operational complexity manageable for the platform and sales/legal teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pilot web UI + API toggle to enable SLA on-demand for a route with entitlement token issuance. 2) Retention credits assigned to routes and consumed/visible in Console. 3) Questionnaire-to-entitlement mapping enforces compliance pack prerequisites before SLA can be purchased. 4) Billing records show correct monthly/prorated charges for activated SLA and consumed retention credits. 5) No customer-facing incidents attributable to the pilot in the first 30 days for pilot customers.
success_metrics: - Conversion of pilot offers to paid add-ons >= 12% within 90 days. - Median time to enable SLA for pilot customers <= 24 hours from approval. - Revenue uplift from participating customers >= $10k ARR per pilot cohort. - Questionnaire pass rate and time-to-approve tracked; target < 5 business days median. - No more than 1 support escalation per 100 enabled routes related to entitlement billing.
experiment_design: Select 8 pilot customers across three buckets (small enterprise, scale-up, platform team). Two cohorts: gated (must complete security questionnaire before enablement) and self-serve (can enable SLA pending automated checks, with manual review fallback). Measure adoption, operational load, billing correctness, and incidence of policy failures. Run for 90 days or until statistical thresholds are reached.
pricing_model: Hybrid model: monthly base fee for SLA on-demand (tiered: $2k/month route-level for enterprise, $500/month for scale-up), plus per-GB-month observability credit consumption priced at $0.12/GB-month for retention beyond default 7 days. Short-term bursts (<=7 days) available as one-time top-ups at 1.5x base per-GB rate. Billing supports prorations and manual credits for pilot reconciliation.
questionnaire_mapping: Security questionnaire outputs map to a small matrix of entitlements: (A) allow SLA purchase, (B) require contract addendum and SOC review, (C) block retention >30 days. Mapping rules stored in Confluence and replicated to the entitlement service as rule sets. Key signals: data residency, encryption at rest key ownership, incident response SLA acceptance, and third-party audit status.
implementation_notes: Engineering to provide: API flag (routes.sla_on_demand), entitlement token service integration, billing hooks for line-item charges, and console UI for credit top-ups and questionnaire state. Design to deliver compact enablement flow in Console and an email-based approval path. Legal to draft addendum template and automated contract link. Observability team to expose retention consumption per-route and aggregate telemetry for pilot dashboards.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: SLA misuse leading to unmet SLOs. Mitigation: limit pilot to routes with historical <10% P99 latency variance; include automatic fallback to standard model on overload. - Risk: Billing disputes. Mitigation: clear line-item detail in invoice and nightly reconciler job; pilot credit reserve to cover disputes. - Risk: Questionnaire friction reduces conversions. Mitigation: provide concierge assistance for gated cohort and pre-fill defaults from account metadata.
